source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: K · Long Island had the highest average price at $51.60/MWh, followed by J · New York City ($47.05/MWh) and F · Capital ($45.20/MWh).
K · Long Island's average price was $15.51/MWh above the cheapest zone, A · West ($36.09/MWh).
K · Long Island had the heaviest congestion: on average it added $10.44/MWh to the price, ahead of J · New York City ($6.13/MWh) and F · Capital ($5.18/MWh).
Congestion lowered the average price in A · West (by $0.78/MWh) and D · North (by $0.85/MWh), consistent with power being trapped on the generating side of transmission limits.
All 3 highest-price zones are also among the 3 most congested: K · Long Island, J · New York City and F · Capital.
Across all zone-months, heavier congestion tends to come with higher prices: a moderate correlation (r = -0.45).
The link is strongest in NYC & Long Island (J–K) (r = -0.62) and weakest in Upstate (A–E) (r = 0.01).
The most extreme single 5-minute congestion value was -$5,147.04/MWh in K · Long Island (Jun 2025), far beyond its monthly average.
cannot_conclude: Higher congestion in a zone does not tell us which transmission line was the bottleneck.
Congestion and price moving together does not prove congestion caused the higher price; weather, fuel prices and demand affect both.
Average $/MWh cannot be turned into total dollars paid, because zone electricity usage is not in this data.
data_notes: D · North: congestion is exactly 0 for all of December 2025 (average, minimum and maximum). This may be a data gap, so that month is not interpreted.
